guide.summary: You must create your own Shopify app even to prototype, because Composio has no managed Shopify app. For one store (or one Plus org) it is easy: create an app in the Dev Dashboard, use custom distribution, and wait on nothing except an optional read_all_orders approval. Serving many merchants needs public distribution and Shopify app review (a merchant-facing UI, install started from Shopify, protected customer data review), and the review has no official timeline.

composio.note: Bring your own app. The toolkit supports OAUTH2 and S2S_OAUTH2; the connection flow asks for the store subdomain. What S2S_OAUTH2 requires is not documented on the toolkit page.

need_own_app.answer: Yes, always. Composio has no managed Shopify app, so even a dev store needs your own app.
reasons: Each app is tied to a distribution method: custom (one store or Plus org) or public (App Store review)
Protected customer data and read_all_orders are granted per app
Your app name appears on the merchant's install/permissions screen

scenarios.label: Prototype on your own dev store
scenarios.when_this_applies: You are building or demoing the agent and only need test data. Composio has no managed Shopify app, so even this needs your own app.

hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count (account, dev store, app, version, Composio auth config, connect), not measured. c11, c14

waiting.basis: Dev stores need no review, including for protected customer data (c37). read_all_orders still needs approval (c42) if you need orders older than 60 days.

scenarios.approval: None. To read orders/customer fields in a Partner-org app you must first pick a distribution method (c36), which is permanent (c17), so use a separate dev app.

scenarios.label: One merchant store (custom app)
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your agent serves a single merchant (or one Plus org with several stores). No App Store listing, no app review.

hands_on.basis: Estimate from step count: s1 setup plus selecting custom distribution, generating an install link, and the merchant installing/connecting. Not measured. c19, c21

waiting.estimate: None for distribution; Unknown if you need read_all_orders
waiting.basis: Custom distribution needs no approval (c19/c21) and protected customer data is always available to custom apps (c34). read_all_orders approval time is undocumented (c58).

scenarios.approval: No app review. Protected customer data: always available for custom apps (c34). read_all_orders: request in Partner Dashboard (c42).
extras: Orders older than 60 days need approval

scenarios.label: Many merchants (public app)
scenarios.when_this_applies: Arbitrary merchants should be able to connect their store to your agent product.

hands_on.basis: App Store apps need a merchant-facing UI (c28), install initiated from Shopify with immediate OAuth (c26, c27), compliance webhooks (c29), a listing and icon (c31), and protected-data requests (c40). Estimate from scope of work, not measured.

waiting.estimate: Unknown officially; reports range from ~3 weeks to over 4 weeks per review round
waiting.basis: No official timeline (c55). Shopify staff reply in 2025 said ~3 weeks (c53, reported); developers in April 2026 reported 4+ weeks (c54, reported). Rejections add rounds.

scenarios.approval: Shopify app review (c24), same rules for listed and limited-visibility apps (c25). Protected customer data review for orders/customers (c33, c34); level 2 adds data protection reviews (c35).
scenarios.shortcut: Serving one merchant? A custom app needs no review.

scenarios.label: A few merchants, one app each
scenarios.when_this_applies: You onboard a few merchants by hand (agency-style) and want to avoid app review.

hands_on.basis: Custom distribution covers only one store or one Plus org per app (c19, c20), so each merchant needs its own app, install link, and Composio auth config. Estimate from step count, not measured.

waiting.basis: Custom distribution has no review (c21); read_all_orders approval time undocumented (c58).

scenarios.approval: None for distribution. read_all_orders per app if needed (c42).

prerequisites.title: Shopify account with developer access
prerequisites.detail: A Shopify Partner account (Partner organization) or the App developer role in the merchant's organization. A Partner org is needed to pick a distribution method and to use Partner Dashboard access requests (protected customer data, read_all_orders).

prerequisites.title: A store to install on
prerequisites.detail: A dev store for prototyping (max 250 per org), or the merchant's store domain for custom distribution.

prerequisites.title: Composio project and dashboard access
prerequisites.detail: You create a Shopify auth config with your own client ID/secret and copy the redirect URI the dashboard shows.

prerequisites.title: A scope list
prerequisites.detail: Know which Admin API scopes the agent needs, which are protected customer data (orders, customers), and whether you need orders older than 60 days.

prerequisites.title: App Store requirements
prerequisites.detail: A merchant-facing UI, compliance webhooks, a 1200x1200 icon, listing content, privacy/data-protection details, and an install flow that starts from Shopify.

steps.title: Pick the scenario and draft the scope list
steps.detail: List the Admin API scopes the agent's tools need. Flag protected customer data (orders, customers, fulfillment), approval-required scopes like read_all_orders, and fields needing level 2 (name, email, phone, address). Recommend custom vs public distribution.
inputs: What the agent should read/write in Shopify
steps.done_when: You have a minimal scope list and a chosen scenario.

steps.title: Get developer access
steps.detail: Sign up for a Shopify Partner account (needed for distribution choice and access requests), or have the merchant grant you the App developer role in their organization.
steps.done_when: dev.shopify.com/dashboard opens on Home, not 'Your account doesn't have developer access yet'.

steps.title: Create a dev store
steps.detail: Dev Dashboard > Stores > Create store > Dev, or `shopify store create dev --demo-data`. Use it for testing in every scenario.
inputs: Store name (the myshopify URL can't be changed later)
steps.done_when: The store shows in the Dev Dashboard Stores list and you can log in.

steps.title: Create the Shopify app
steps.detail: Dev Dashboard > Apps > Create app > Start from Dev Dashboard (fine for an API-only agent integration). For an App Store app, scaffold with `shopify app init` (Shopify CLI) since you need a UI. Keep a separate dev app if you will select a distribution method.
steps.done_when: The app appears in the Dev Dashboard Apps list.

steps.title: Start a Composio auth config and copy its redirect URI
steps.detail: Composio dashboard > Create Auth Config > Shopify > OAuth2 > use your own developer credentials. Copy the redirect/callback URI shown there; do not use one from a tutorial.
steps.done_when: You have the Composio redirect URI copied.

steps.title: Configure and release an app version
steps.detail: On the app's Versions page set App URL (non-embedded apps can use the default), the scopes from step 1, and the redirect URL from Composio (must match exactly). Do not include read_all_orders or other approval-required scopes until approved, or version creation fails. Click Release. An agent can write the shopify.app.toml for CLI apps.
steps.done_when: A version is active on the app.

steps.title: Put the client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Copy Client ID and Client secret from the app's Settings in the Dev Dashboard into the Composio auth config and create it. Note the auth config ID (ac_...).
steps.done_when: Composio shows the auth config with an ac_ ID.

steps.title: Connect the dev store through Composio
steps.detail: In Composio, Connect Account, enter the store subdomain (the part before .myshopify.com), and approve the install in Shopify. The authorize URL is per store, so a wrong subdomain gives 'Store unavailable'; a wrong client ID only shows after store login.
steps.done_when: The connected account shows Active in Composio.

steps.title: Wire the auth config into your agent and smoke-test
steps.detail: Pass the auth config ID in the session's authConfigs for shopify, run a read tool (products, then orders), and check GraphQL responses for an errors entry on redacted protected fields.
steps.done_when: A product read and an order read return data (or expected redactions are understood).

steps.title: Select the distribution method on the production app
steps.detail: Dev Dashboard > app Home > Distribution > Select distribution method. Custom for one store/Plus org; Public for many merchants. This is permanent. If the app was created in a store's own organization there is no Distribution card; install from the Installs card.
steps.done_when: The Distribution card links to 'Manage custom install link' or 'Manage Shopify App Store listing'.

steps.title: Draft protected customer data justifications
steps.detail: Write per-field reasons (name, email, phone, address) tied to agent features, a retention policy, and a checklist against Shopify's level 1/2 requirements.
inputs: Data flow of your agent (what is stored, where, how long)
steps.done_when: Reasons and data-protection answers are ready to paste.

steps.title: Request protected customer data access and fields
steps.detail: Partner Dashboard > Apps > your app > API access requests > Protected customer data access. Select data and fields, paste reasons. Dev-store-only and custom apps don't need review; public apps do, and you can't apply while under review.
steps.done_when: Fields are selected; for public apps, data protection details are complete before submitting.

steps.title: Request read_all_orders (only if you need orders older than 60 days)
steps.detail: Partner Dashboard > Apps > your app > API access requests > Read all orders scope > Request access, describing your app. After approval add it to a new version next to read_orders/write_orders; merchants must re-approve scopes.

steps.title: Wait for read_all_orders approval
steps.done_when: Shopify approves; you can add read_all_orders to a version without an app_access error.

steps.title: Generate a custom install link for the merchant
steps.detail: Enter the merchant's myshopify.com or admin.shopify.com domain, optionally allow multi-store installs for one Plus org, generate and send the link. After install, the merchant (or you, with their login) connects through Composio with the store subdomain. For s4, repeat per merchant with a separate app and Composio auth config.
steps.done_when: Merchant has installed the app and the Composio connection is Active.

steps.title: Build App Store requirements
steps.detail: Implement a merchant-facing UI (embedded via App Bridge), an install flow that starts from Shopify and runs OAuth immediately with no manual shop-domain entry and no pop-up OAuth, compliance webhooks, and expiring offline tokens. Decide how this install flow hands off to Composio's connection (undocumented).
steps.done_when: Automated checks on the App Store review page pass.

steps.title: Prepare listing and submit for review
steps.detail: Complete configuration (URLs, compliance webhooks, 1200x1200 icon, API contact, emergency contact), create the listing, finish protected customer data, run automated checks, and click Submit. Agent can draft listing copy and test instructions.
steps.done_when: App status is Submitted and you got the confirmation email.

steps.title: Wait for app review
steps.detail: Status moves Submitted > (Paused if core issues) > Reviewed > Published. Reply to reviewer emails promptly.
steps.done_when: Status is Published (or approved with limited visibility).

traps.title: Composio's connect flow vs App Store install rules
traps.detail: Composio asks for the store subdomain; the App Store forbids manual shop-domain entry and requires install from a Shopify surface, and discourages pop-up OAuth.

traps.title: App Store requires a real UI
traps.detail: A headless agent integration is not enough for public distribution.

traps.title: You can't even prototype without your own app
traps.detail: Composio has no managed Shopify app. The toolkit FAQ mentions a 'default Shopify OAuth app' but the toolkit is listed as bring-your-own; plan on creating an app from day one.

traps.title: Custom distribution is one merchant per app
traps.detail: One store or one Plus org per app. Serving several merchants this way means one app and one Composio auth config per merchant.

traps.title: Old tutorials: 'Apps > Develop apps' in the admin
traps.detail: Admin-created custom apps (pre-generated shpat tokens) can no longer be created. Use the Dev Dashboard or Shopify CLI.

traps.title: Distribution choice is permanent
traps.detail: Selecting custom or public can't be undone, and you must select one before requesting protected customer data even for dev stores. Use a separate dev app and choose on the production app.

traps.title: Orders silently stop at 60 days
traps.detail: read_orders/write_orders only cover the last 60 days. read_all_orders needs Shopify approval, and declaring it early breaks version creation.

traps.title: Redacted data looks like success
traps.detail: Unapproved protected fields come back null with an errors entry in a 200 response. An agent may read 'no email' instead of 'not approved'.

traps.title: Scope changes don't reach existing installs
traps.detail: Adding scopes in a new version requires each merchant to approve them; existing Composio connections may need reconnecting.

traps.title: Client credentials only for your own organization
traps.detail: The no-consent client credentials grant (likely what S2S fits) fails on stores outside your org, including client stores.

blockers.symptom: App review stuck in Submitted, Paused, or Reviewed
blockers.what_it_means: Core requirements unmet (Paused) or reviewer needs fixes (Reviewed); otherwise queue time.
blockers.what_to_do: Fix issues and resubmit; reply to reviewer emails; protected data can't be changed during review.
blockers.agent_can_help: Run the requirements checklist against your app and draft replies.

blockers.symptom: Creating an app version fails with an app_access validation error on scopes
blockers.what_it_means: You declared an approval-required scope (e.g. read_all_orders) before Shopify approved it.
blockers.what_to_do: Remove the scope, release, request access in Partner Dashboard > API access requests, add it after approval.
blockers.agent_can_help: Diff your scope list against the 'Shopify approval required' scopes and draft the request text.

blockers.symptom: GraphQL returns null customer fields plus 'This app is not approved to access the Customer object'
blockers.what_it_means: Protected customer data or fields weren't selected/approved for this app.
blockers.what_to_do: Select distribution method, then request the data and fields in Partner Dashboard (custom apps: always available; public apps: reviewed).
blockers.agent_can_help: Detect the errors entry and draft per-field justifications.

blockers.symptom: Order reads/updates 403, or no orders older than 60 days
blockers.what_to_do: Request read_all_orders, add it to a new version, have the merchant re-approve, reconnect in Composio.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the connection's granted scopes and draft the access request.

blockers.symptom: Oauth error shop_not_permitted: Client credentials cannot be performed on this shop
blockers.what_it_means: Client credentials only works when app and store are in the same organization.
blockers.what_to_do: Use OAuth2 (authorization code) with custom distribution for client stores.
blockers.agent_can_help: Explain which grant fits and switch the Composio auth scheme.

blockers.symptom: No Distribution card on the app's Home
blockers.what_it_means: The app was created in a store's organization, not a Partner organization.
blockers.what_to_do: Install from the Installs card for that one store, or recreate the app in a Partner organization if you need custom/public distribution.

blockers.what_it_means: The store subdomain entered in Composio is wrong; authorize URLs are per store.
blockers.what_to_do: Use the exact myshopify subdomain (e.g. abc123 from abc123.myshopify.com).
blockers.agent_can_help: Validate the subdomain format before starting the connection.

blockers.symptom: 'App not found' when connecting Shopify in Composio
blockers.what_it_means: Per Composio's FAQ, a default Shopify OAuth app is unavailable.
blockers.what_to_do: Use your own Shopify app credentials in a custom auth config.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check that the session passes your auth config ID.

open_questions: What fields Composio's S2S_OAUTH2 scheme takes for Shopify, and whether it uses Shopify's client credentials grant (same-org only). Check the Composio dashboard's Shopify auth config form or ask Composio.

Whether a Composio-hosted connection can satisfy App Store requirement 2.3.1 (install from a Shopify surface, no manual shop domain). Likely needs your own install entry point that passes the shop to Composio; test with a limited-visibility public app.
Official turnaround for read_all_orders requests and for app review. Only community reports exist (~3 to 4+ weeks for review).
How protected customer data fields are selected for an app created in a store's own organization (no Distribution card). Test hands-on.
Whether Composio requests expiring offline tokens and handles Shopify refresh tokens. Check a connected account's token metadata.
Whether a Partner account has any cost (not stated on the pages fetched).

guide.verdict: An hour or two for one store, with no review. Serving many merchants means Shopify app review, which has no published timeline.
